avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Folic Acid (>5mg daily)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Folic acid directly antagonizes trimethoprim's antibacterial mechanism; high doses may reduce drug efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose supplementation during treatment; standard prenatal doses (400-800mcg) are acceptable

avoid_supplements.name: ACE inhibitor herbs (Licorice root)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Trimethoprim can cause hyperkalemia; licorice causes sodium retention and potassium depletion, creating unpredictable electrolyte effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid licorice supplements during trimethoprim use; monitor potassium levels

avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements/high-dose potassium
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Trimethoprim inhibits renal potassium excretion via ROMK channels, significantly increasing hyperkalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; obtain baseline potassium level and renal function; monitor K+ weekly during treatment

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin B12
caution_supplements.mechanism: Trimethoprim inhibits folate metabolism, which indirectly affects B12-dependent processes; supplementation may help prevent deficiency
caution_supplements.action: Consider supplementation if treatment exceeds 2 weeks; baseline B12 levels recommended for prolonged use

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have minor interaction with renal handling; generally safe but monitor with other electrolytes
caution_supplements.action: Use standard doses; obtain baseline magnesium if on prolonged therapy

avoid_foods.name: High potassium foods (bananas, spinach, sweet potatoes, avocado, coconut water)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Trimethoprim reduces renal potassium excretion; excessive dietary potassium increases hyperkalemia risk
avoid_foods.action: Limit high-potassium foods during treatment; provide patient with potassium-restricted food list if renal impairment present

caution_foods.name: Leafy greens (moderate amounts)
caution_foods.mechanism: Folate content may theoretically reduce drug efficacy, though dietary folate levels are typically insufficient to cause clinically significant antagonism
caution_foods.action: Moderate consumption is acceptable; avoid intentional supplementation of these foods

caution_foods.name: Dairy products
caution_foods.mechanism: May slightly reduce trimethoprim absorption; minimal clinical impact with standard dosing
caution_foods.action: Space administration at least 2 hours apart from calcium-rich foods if absorption is critical

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum potassium, creatinine, and BUN at baseline and weekly during treatment, particularly in elderly or renally impaired patients. Assess for folate deficiency signs (macrocytic anemia, neuropathy) in patients on prolonged therapy >2 weeks.
